evidence: introspect_pm_token (routes/sso.rs:729-786) caches PM token-introspection results in state.token_cache (TokenValidationCache, 60s TTL, 10000 entries -- state.rs:947 `TokenValidationCache::new(60, 10000)`). On the FAILURE branch at routes/sso.rs:759-766, when the PM introspection endpoint returns a NON-SUCCESS HTTP status (`if !response.status().is_success()`), the code does `state.token_cache.set(token, false, None, None).await` (sso.rs:762) and then returns Err. This caches active=false for a token whose real status is UNKNOWN.

This conflates two very different conditions. Per RFC 7662, a genuinely inactive token is signalled by HTTP 200 with a body `{"active": false}` (handled correctly further down at sso.rs:770-784). A 4xx/5xx from the introspection endpoint instead means a client-config or upstream error -- PM API down/redeploying, a 502/503 from its proxy, bad client_credentials, etc. -- and is NOT evidence that the user's token is inactive. Caching false on `!is_success()` treats an upstream outage as an authoritative negative.

The poisoning is observable on SUBSEQUENT requests, not the failing one. The cache-hit path (sso.rs:735-745) returns `Ok(TokenIntrospectionResponse { active: cached.active, .. })` for any non-expired entry with NO error surfaced, and TokenValidationCache::get (state.rs:656-673) returns any entry while `Instant::now() < cached.expires_at` regardless of how it was set (state.rs:675-716 stores `active` with a uniform `ttl_seconds` expiry). So during a PM introspection blip, the first request with a valid token 5xx-fails and writes active=false; every following request with that SAME valid token for up to 60s hits the cache and is told the token is inactive -- denying an otherwise-valid Reality Portal session. Common because a browser fires several API calls per page with the same bearer token.

Impact: availability/correctness defect on the SSO auth hot path -- a transient PM introspection failure (deploy, 5xx, proxy timeout) is amplified into up-to-60s of spurious session denials for valid users. It fails CLOSED (denies rather than grants), so it is not a security bypass, which is why this is scored medium (+2) rather than high.

Fix (self-contained, routes/sso.rs only): populate the cache ONLY from a successfully-parsed 200 introspection body -- cache both active=true and the genuine active=false that PM returns in the JSON. On any transport error or non-2xx status, return Err WITHOUT calling token_cache.set, so the next request re-validates instead of reading a poisoned negative. IG3: unit test that a 503 introspection response leaves state.token_cache empty for that token and that a following 200 introspection re-validates (active=true).

Confidence medium: the set(false)-on-!is_success() -> get()-returns-Ok(active:false)-within-TTL path is confirmed by static read of sso.rs:735-766 and state.rs:656-716; not upgraded to high because runtime confirmation of the exact caller re-entry within the 60s window was not executed (static-only pass).

All three PM-facing SSO helpers construct a brand-new HTTP client per request via `reqwest::Client::new()`: exchange_pm_token (routes/sso.rs:687), get_user_info (routes/sso.rs:711), and introspect_pm_token (routes/sso.rs:748). Each call therefore builds a fresh connection pool and re-runs TLS setup instead of reusing a keep-alive connection to the PM API -- on the SSO login/validation hot path that runs on effectively every authenticated portal request.

More importantly for robustness: `reqwest::Client::new()` applies NO request timeout. A hung or slow PM endpoint (the very outage scenario in the sibling finding) can stall these SSO helpers indefinitely, holding the portal request open. Contrast state.rs:756-762, where PmApiClient::new deliberately builds its reqwest client with `.timeout(Duration::from_secs(timeout_seconds))` -- the timeout discipline exists in the codebase but is not applied to the SSO client calls.

Fix (self-contained): build a single shared `reqwest::Client` once (with an explicit `.timeout(...)`, mirroring PmApiClient) -- either store it on AppState alongside the existing PmApiClient or pass the already-pooled client in -- and reuse it across exchange_pm_token / get_user_info / introspect_pm_token instead of `reqwest::Client::new()` at each call site. IG3: a test asserting the SSO helpers use a client with a configured timeout (or a construction-site assertion that no bare Client::new() remains in sso.rs).

Confidence medium; severity low (+1): the missing pooling is a pure efficiency smell, but the missing timeout is a genuine robustness gap that compounds the introspection-outage scenario, so this is worth landing rather than dropping as a nit. Both aspects are confirmed by static read of the three Client::new() sites vs the timeout-configured PmApiClient.
